metadata_notes.hub_param_count: HF's auto-generated Safetensors section reports 25 959 006 099 (~26 B) for this pack. That is a count of stored tensor units in the headers, not parameters: HF weighs U32 blocks x4 (right for the FP8 E4M3FN trunk, four 8-bit weights per U32) and U16 blocks x1 (wrong for EXL3, ~6.095 weights per 16-bit unit at k=2.625), so the figure mixes units. Parsing all 52 shard headers ourselves gives 22 388 758 419 stored elements. HF's per-dtype lines are inconsistent with the headers in their own way: U16/F16/I64 match exactly, U32 is 4x (packed 8-bit codes), and BF16 is short by 155 228 160 (519 896 944 vs 675 125 104) even though model.safetensors.index.json indexes every tensor in every shard (verified: header BF16 == index BF16, 0 tensors missing). HF's quirk is reproduced but not explained; the arithmetic above reads the shard headers directly.
metadata_notes.logical_parameters: U16 20 230 963 200 x 16/2.625 = 123.31 B (EXL3 experts, 48 layers + MTP) + U32 1 241 825 280 x 4 = 4.97 B (trunk, 8-bit affine group 64: four 8-bit codes per U32, e.g. embed_tokens.weight stored [248320, 640] for hidden 2560) + BF16 675 125 104 = 0.675 B + ngram_table.bin 20 000 000 x 2560 = 51.20 B (4-bit affine group 32; 32.00 GB / 51.2 B = 5.0 bits/entry with scales) = ~180.16 B logical parameters. The base model (ukisai/Swift1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) counts 179 999 981 424 on the Hub, so the pack agrees within +0.086 %. F16 240 844 800 units are scales, not weights. Quote ~180 B parameters for this model.
metadata_notes.config_json: config.json still declares quantization_config {bits: 8, group_size: 64, mode: affine}, which is why the Hub shows an 8-bit chip. sushi validates quantization_config at load (its own errors: "unsupported quantization mode '' (supported: affine, nvfp4, mxfp4, mxfp8)" and "unsupported affine quantization: -bit"), and the record describes the affine dense arm, not the 2.625 expert rate. Rewriting bits/mode risks an unloadable pack, so the converter's config.json is shipped untouched and the card explains the chip.

kld_divergence.reading: cross rows compare two quantisations of two DIFFERENT models (Swift 1.5 vs base Qwen) and include the kv8 penalty; they are a divergence fingerprint, not a KLD-to-teacher, and are not comparable with the reference_bar_from_sushi_docs protocol (16x512 wikitext). Ours-vs-theirs 0.0758 and theirs-vs-ours 0.0954 to first EOS; both are below the 0.1355 that a single 2.6bpw pack sits from its own BF16 teacher on sushi's fixture.

measurements_task_eval: measurements.json task_eval + measurements/eval/*-manifest.json; six clean rows, arms matched (greedy t=0, effort medium on code / xhigh on hard, concurrency 2, cap 16000, identical server flags, only --model moves): ours code 81/100, theirs code 86/100, ours hard 36/50, theirs hard 36/50, and the 10-question Olympiad slice at budgeted arms (--reasoning-budget 4096, a separate launcher): ours 1/10, theirs 2/10. Slice rows are a different deck size and are labelled as such; they are not deck scores. Hard-deck rows carry 12/50 and 13/50 cases that reasoned with no Answer: line (cases_without_final_text, kept as real results): validity is outputTokens == 0, so the only artifact is invalid/ (0/100 at 0 generated tokens in 3.1 s, the server answering with no pack resident) and superseded/ holds the shared-engine 82/100 pilot. OlympiadBench 0/10 on BOTH packs is an output-channel failure, not hidden competence. beamster's claimed Hard-50 88.0 % measures 72.0 % with their pack on this server. NOT RUN: --eval-suite core (92: GPQA Diamond, SuperGPQA, AIME 2025, COMPSEC), skipped on cost (~3-5 h per pack) — no GPQA/AIME/SuperGPQA/COMPSEC number on the card is our measurement.
